creator: OMB Gaming
move: Video opens mid-arrest with no channel intro: he plays the officer live, calling the fleeing suspect and narrating his own tool choice and missed first attempt as in-world action, then talks the suspect down once cuffed
timing: zero preamble, commentary starts with the action and runs at chase speed, verdict on the arrest delivered within seconds of the catch
phrasing_shape: short in-character callout, repeated status word while running, plain recap once the suspect is secured
aggregate_note: Likely generalises across roleplay channels: immersion from frame one is a format choice, not a personality trait

creator: OMB Gaming
move: Shifts to scouting and initiates the next scene himself: names a vantage point, the reason for it, the gear to bring, and invites teammates to follow him on foot rather than waiting to be assigned
timing: plan stated before anyone moves, unhurried briefing pace after the chase peak
phrasing_shape: place, reason, equipment, open invitation to the team
aggregate_note: Plausibly generalises: in group roleplay the host usually doubles as scene initiator and movement director

creator: OMB Gaming
move: Delivers the whole video premise as an in-world briefing: why the team is here, what the target site is, what informants reported, and that a raid is scheduled for the night, all framed as stakes for the operation rather than as a video description
timing: one continuous exposition hold of roughly a minute during slow scouting movement
phrasing_shape: mission reason, target description, history of evidence, tonight's objective
aggregate_note: Strong candidate pattern: roleplayers smuggle audience exposition inside character briefings so the fourth wall never opens

creator: OMB Gaming
move: Runs drone reconnaissance and narrates only what the feed can actually show, openly stating range and zoom limits and refusing to push closer because the in-world team could be spotted
timing: slow observational pace, pauses while panning, limits admitted in real time as they appear
phrasing_shape: what I can see, what I cannot see, why we stop here
aggregate_note: Witnessed-only knowledge is the architectural question (role-010, field lean 78): this is a clear single-video instance of a creator choosing it

creator: OMB Gaming
move: States the full infiltration plan in character: avoid the patrolled road, take the river by boat, cross a short stretch of ground, cut the fence, enter the site, with the failure condition named in advance
timing: plan delivered in one pass just after recon ends, before any movement starts
phrasing_shape: route step by step, distance estimate, entry action, if-nothing-goes-wrong qualifier
aggregate_note: Likely generalises to heist and raid formats in any game: the plan said in character is both strategy and trailer for the scene

creator: OMB Gaming
move: A teammate has lost the reconnaissance drone near the target: he reacts with a brief exasperated joke at the teammate's expense, then immediately re-tasks the whole group back to the van and the next step instead of dwelling on it
timing: character cracks for only a few seconds, task language resumes within the same breath
phrasing_shape: one disbelieving question, short laugh, immediate regroup instruction
aggregate_note: Useful general pattern: a short, bounded break that is absorbed back into the scene rather than ending it

creator: OMB Gaming
move: Convenes a formal joint briefing and directs allied players like a commander: assigns the sheriff team their vehicles, entry roads and blocking job, sets a timed delay after the breach signal, fixes the start time, then formally dismisses everyone to eat and rest until the hour
timing: several minutes of pure planning register, no action competing with it, ends with a clear muster time
phrasing_shape: thanks, your task, your position, your trigger signal, dismissal with return time
aggregate_note: Directing other players at this scale is the distinctive OMB skill; expect weaker versions wherever one host runs a recording team

creator: OMB Gaming
move: At the breach he switches to pure coordination: confirms each tower guard is down in short repeated status calls, waits for the full confirmation, then issues the push order and keeps naming the next objective as the team advances
timing: reaction latency near zero, calls land on the events, density spikes to almost continuous short phrases
phrasing_shape: status count repeated, hold, release order, next target named
aggregate_note: Likely generalises across squad roleplay: under fire the host becomes a switchboard, not a narrator

creator: OMB Gaming
move: Aftermath is played for in-world consequence rather than celebration: he notes the cost of taking no prisoners for the later case, orders one more sweep, credits the allied team by name of unit, and walks the group to the entrance for a debrief
timing: pace drops immediately after the last shot, reflective hold of about half a minute, no victory lap
phrasing_shape: what it costs us, one more check, credit to the team, where we debrief
aggregate_note: Consequence-first aftermath matches role-011 stakes framing; compare against creators who treat a win as pure confetti

creator: Jesse Gillett
move: States the experiment premise up front: two community-made variants of a known destructible airliner will be tested for how well they crash, with credit and pointers given to the mod makers before any flight
timing: premise complete inside the first seconds, test subjects introduced one at a time over the first minute
phrasing_shape: what we are testing, why this test bed, credit to the makers, first subject
aggregate_note: Premise-first openings are the Show-mode norm (coach-026 field lean 80); this is a textbook instance

creator: Jesse Gillett
move: At the crash moment he announces he is letting go of the controls and switches roles from pilot to witness: the play-by-play simply tracks what the physics does to the aircraft, the other plane and the hangar
timing: hands-off declared just before impact, commentary latency near zero during the few seconds of destruction, short verdict right after
phrasing_shape: release stated, event chain called as it happens, one amazement verdict
aggregate_note: The core narrate-versus-witness move: the performer schedules his own helplessness so the simulation becomes the actor

creator: Jesse Gillett
move: Walks the crash site slowly like an investigator, cataloguing separated parts, fire damage and debris spread, and only then delivers the comparison verdict on the first variant
timing: longest hold in the video so far, roughly half a minute of inspection before any verdict
phrasing_shape: point at part, what broke and where it landed, repeated, then summary judgement
aggregate_note: The forensic tour is this channel's payoff ritual; expect a version of it in most destruction channels, usually shorter

creator: Jesse Gillett
move: Second aircraft sheds parts on takeoff and he corrects his own live misreading on camera, changing his identification of what fell off, then converts the surprise into a prediction: the extra thrust is making it fast enough to tear itself apart
timing: correction lands within seconds of the event, prediction follows immediately and is tested over the next minute
phrasing_shape: alarm, self-correction, cause guess, escalating prediction
aggregate_note: Open self-correction is a trust pattern (coach-035 field lean 78) that costs nothing and is easy for an avatar to copy structurally

creator: Jesse Gillett
move: Thanks a commenter for pointing him at the variants being tested, then deliberately repeats the same crash with the second aircraft so the comparison stays fair, naming the control he is trying to keep constant
timing: gratitude placed in the reset gap, method restated before the repeat run
phrasing_shape: credit to the viewer, same test again, what will be held equal, what may differ
aggregate_note: Audience-sourced test subjects plus controlled repeats: a small channel behaving like a lab, worth flagging as a question-miner candidate on method narration

creator: Jesse Gillett
move: Engineers a set piece: a luggage vehicle stopped on the runway with cargo spilling, framed with mock sympathy for its crew, then flies the aircraft at it to see the outcome he has staged
timing: setup narrated slowly and completely before the run starts, outcome allowed to play without interruption
phrasing_shape: scene described, victim framed, aircraft launched, result witnessed
aggregate_note: Engineered set pieces over emergent play is spectacle-001 (field lean 68); this channel sits near the engineered end

creator: Jesse Gillett
move: After surviving the attack run and landing, the celebration is a single disbelief beat, then he exits the aircraft and spends far longer touring the damage, reading holes and leaks as a story of how the flight nearly ended
timing: celebration under ten seconds, damage tour several times longer
phrasing_shape: disbelief line, exit, damage item, what it would have meant, repeated
aggregate_note: Short celebration plus long savouring matches coach-012's low field lean: the inspection is the reward, not the cheer

creator: Jesse Gillett
move: Closes with a finale no gameplay required: rebuilds the burnt fuselage with the physics tool into a cross-section, compares the method to real accident investigation in paraphrase, and walks the fire's path through the cabin as the video's concluding evidence
timing: slowest segment of the video, held to the final seconds with no new action introduced
phrasing_shape: reconstruction shown, real-world parallel named, burn path traced, sign-off
aggregate_note: A post-mortem as finale is a strong channel signature; whether it generalises depends on the other physics channels, see Neotastic entries
